rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction before the final trait marks forbidding wrong as especially difficult, since it can bring humiliation or even death; the preceding traits are closer to one another.
rows.anchor: النهي عن المنكر يكون أشدّ على الإنسان وقد يؤدي إلى الإهانة والقتل أحياناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first Dhu al-Qarnayn pursuit follows his empowerment immediately, while later expeditions follow one another over time; fa suits the first and thumma the later pursuits.
rows.anchor: الفاء تفيد الترتيب والتعقيب. وثمّ تفيد الترتيب والتراخي أي تكون المدة أطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, akhsar means greater loss than khasir, so the comparative form marks a more severe degree of loss.
rows.anchor: وفي اللغة الأخسر هو أكثر خسراناً من الخاسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described in Hud block both themselves and others from God's path, unlike those in Nahl who block only themselves; they are therefore more grievously lost.
rows.anchor: الذي يصدّ نفسه وغيره عن سبيل الله أخسر من الذي صدّ نفسه عن سبيل الله لوحده فقط

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Grammarians explain la jarama as an oath, or as meaning truly/rightfully; each reading gives emphasis.
rows.anchor: عند النحاة تعني القسم أو بمعنى حقاً أو حقَّ وكلها تدل على التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud adds several charges beyond Naml, including blocking God's path and lying against God, so it emphatically calls its offenders the worst losers; Naml lacks that added emphasis.
rows.anchor: فقد زاد على ذلك أنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله وأنهم يفترون على الله الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's prior knowledge records destiny; later knowledge brings that decree to realization and concerns recompense, while human action confirms the prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: علم سابق الذي سجّل فيه الله تعالى القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads li-na'lama ayy al-hizbayn as making clear which group knows the truth about the youths' duration, rather than implying that God learns something previously unknown.
rows.anchor: لنعلم أي الحزبين يعني لنعلم أي منهم يعلم الحقيقة لأن كل قسم قال شيئاً فمن الذي يعلم الحقيقة؟ الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to say tomorrow fits the occasion: when asked three questions, including about the Cave youths, the Prophet promised an answer the next day, but revelation was delayed fifteen nights and rumors spread.
rows.anchor: سُئل رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن ثلاثة أسئلة من قبل الكفار منها عن أهل الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion does not limit the verse to one case; the parallel command about coercing women addressed Abdullah ibn Ubayy's attempt to force women who wanted chastity, while other texts clarify the broader issue.
rows.anchor: الحادثة التي حصلت أن عبد الله بن أبيّ أراد إكراههن وهن يردن التحصّن فذكر المسألة كما هي واقعة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi describes the Quran's parts as connected and harmonious like a single word, supporting a link between the endings and beginnings of neighboring surahs.
rows.anchor: هو كالكلمة الواحدة في توافقه وإتصال بعضه ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah's account of God hearing Khawla bint Tha'laba's complaint against Aws ibn al-Samit illustrates the great divine favor named at the end of Hadid; the Prophet had offered her no remedy.
rows.anchor: جبار السموات والأرض ملك الملوك يسمع لخولة بنت ثعلبة تجادل في زوجها أوس ابن الصامت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of hears rather than knows signals nearness: one can know about something from far away, whereas hearing conveys proximity; Hadid also says God knows what enters and leaves the earth.
rows.anchor: أما السمع فيدل على القُرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadid's recurring language concerns God's knowledge and observation, while Saba's recurring atmosphere concerns the afterlife; the repeated vocabulary shapes each surah's tone.
rows.anchor: جو السورة يتردد فيه العلم. في سورة سبأ الذي شاع في جو السورة ذِكر الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadid 57:7 commands two things, faith in God and His Messenger and spending; these two themes broadly characterize the surah.
rows.anchor: أمرهم بشيئين: الإيمان بالله والرسول والإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah repeatedly stresses faith in God and His messengers, rather than listing all pillars of faith.
rows.anchor: الإيمان بالله والرسول لم يذكر أركان الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending, rather than good works in general, is the surah's distinctive charitable theme; it mentions fighting and martyrs but does not command fighting.
rows.anchor: ومع أنه ذكر القتال لكنه لم يأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah narrows the faith theme to belief in God and His Messenger, repeating it instead of enumerating all the pillars of faith.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر جميع أركان الإيمان في السورة وإنما كرر الإيمان بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It likewise highlights spending rather than good works generally; fighting is mentioned without being commanded, and martyrs and God's helpers appear in related contexts.
rows.anchor: وذكر القتال لكن لم يأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadid's general work theme is spending, and min marks giving from only a portion of the wealth entrusted to people; those who believe and spend receive a great reward.
rows.anchor: فنحن مستخلفون في هذه الأموال إستخلفنا فيها وستذهب إلى غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief opposes faith in God, while denying God's signs opposes faith in His messengers because the signs are conveyed through them.
rows.anchor: كفروا بمقابل الذين آمنوا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the martyrs after the truthful matches the ordering in Nisa; reward and light recur throughout Hadid as its characteristic motifs.
rows.anchor: الأجر والنور واضحان في السورة يترددان في أكثر من موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified verb disbelieved is deliberately general: rejecting revelation makes one an unbeliever even if one believes in God, so the verse does not specify disbelief in God alone.
rows.anchor: فلو آمن بالله وكفر بالرسالات ولم يصدّق سيكون كافراً لذا لم يخصصها وإنما أطلقها عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayaja can describe growth in motion and then drying, but of vegetation it also means to dry; in this verse it means the crop dries and turns yellow.
rows.anchor: هاج تأتي بمعنى يبس وتأتي بمعنى تحرك في النمو ثم يبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to you see it yellow makes the loss of adornment a matter of the observer's sight, since adornment is perceptual; the address applies to every onlooker.
rows.anchor: فتراه مصفراً أي زالت الزينة بالنسبة للناظر لأن الزينة تتعلق بالناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It becomes debris states an objective end with no use; seeing something as debris cannot establish its real value, which depends on knowledge rather than appearance.
rows.anchor: أصبح حطاماً لا فائدة فيه ولا يتعلق برؤيتك له وتقديرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the crop yellow concerns its visible loss of beauty, while its becoming debris states the actual collapse of worldly life, not an observer's judgment.
rows.anchor: فرق بين تراه مصفراً وثم يكون حطاماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa marks immediate sequence, while thumma marks delay: the crop is seen yellow as soon as it dries, but becoming debris takes time; burial follows death promptly whereas resurrection is delayed.
rows.anchor: الفاء للترتيب والتعقيب و (ثم) للترتيب والتراخي أي مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Zumar, God is explicitly the agent who sends water, channels it, brings forth crops, and makes them debris; Hadid only compares worldly life to rain and leaves the agent unstated.
rows.anchor: في آية الحديد ليس هناك إسناد لله تعالى أما في الزمر فالاسناد لله تعالى ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though both words refer to water from the sky, Quranic usage reserves matar for punishment and uses ghayth for beneficial rain; hadith usage can differ.
rows.anchor: في القرآن الكريم يذكر المطر للعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment precedes forgiveness because the gathering and passage by Hell occur before judgment and entry to Paradise; forgiveness then precedes divine approval in Paradise.
rows.anchor: إذن العذاب يسبق المغفرة. وتقديم المغفرة على الرضوان لأنها تسبق الرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse leaves the source of severe punishment unstated but attributes forgiveness to God, emphasizing His mercy; scripture avoids attributing evil to God.
rows.anchor: في المغفرة نسبها له سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghufran appears only as a request for forgiveness from God, in Baqara 2:285; maghfira is not used as a prayer request and appears in statements about forgiveness.
rows.anchor: إذن كلمة غفران مخصصة بطلب المغفرة من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike ghufran, maghfira can come from God or people; the Quran uses it in informative contexts, including forgiveness between people.
rows.anchor: إذن المغفرة ليست خاصة بالله سبحانه وتعالى ولها أكثر من جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ridwan is used only of God and in both seeking and other contexts; mardat is used when seeking someone's pleasure and may concern God or another person.
rows.anchor: الرضوان من الله سبحانه وتعالى فقط ولم ترد في القرآن من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ridwan is the broader term, while mardat is narrower and tied to seeking approval; this is a distinctive Quranic usage.
rows.anchor: الرضوان عام وخاص بالله سبحانه وتعالى والمرضاة أخصّ من الرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After portraying worldly competition in play, boasting, adornment, and accumulation as ending in debris, God redirects people to compete for forgiveness and Paradise.
rows.anchor: فبدل هذه المسابقة في أمور الدنيا التي ستكون حطاماً ألا أدلكم على ما هو خير من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgiveness in 57:20 is a description of worldly life's outcome, so it is from God; 57:21 addresses people with a command, so it says from your Lord.
rows.anchor: في آية مخاطبين والثانية كلام عام وصف للدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah and Lord are names or attributes of the same God, not separate deities, just as the other divine names do not designate separate gods.
rows.anchor: هذه من أسمائه وصفاته التي تذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadid's Paradise is described as like the width of the heaven and earth, while Aal Imran states its width directly; the author concludes the Paradise in Hadid is wider.
rows.anchor: يعني جنة آية الحديد أوسع من جنة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadid offers Paradise to the broad class who believe in God and His messengers, whereas Aal Imran specifies the righteous who spend; the wider class matches the greater width and is called God's great favor.
rows.anchor: في آية الحديد أعدت الجنة للذين آمنوا بالله ورسله وهم أكثر من المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns believers against letting wealth and children distract them from remembering God; whoever does so incurs great loss.
rows.anchor: ومن يفعل ذلك كان خاسراً خسارة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Directly addressing wealth protects believers by forbidding the cause of distraction before it can affect them, and makes the warning more forceful.
rows.anchor: فكأن الله يريد حماية المؤمن وذلك بنهي السبب عن أن يتعرض له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor portrays wealth and children as plotting to ensnare believers, warning them to stay alert rather than become distracted without agency.
rows.anchor: فكأن الأموال والأولاد ينصبون الشرك ليلهوه عن ذ كر الله

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Ruh al-Ma'ani says the prohibition is really directed at people, but addresses wealth because it strongly causes and contributes to distraction.
rows.anchor: روح المعاني) : "والمراد بنهي الأموال وما بعدها نهي المخاطبين، وإنما وجه إليها للمبالغة لأنها لقوة تسببها للهو وشدة مدخليتها فيه

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi explains that directing the prohibition toward wealth and its like is for emphasis.
rows.anchor: تفسير البيضاوي) : "توجيه النهي إليها للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating la before children shows that either wealth or children can distract alone; without it, the wording could imply that only their combination is prohibited.
rows.anchor: كلاً من الأموال والأولاد داع من دواعي الإلهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth precedes children because managing and growing it consumes time and can distract a person from family; children are more valuable since wealth serves them and is left to them.
rows.anchor: فإن الانشغال فيها وفي تنميتها يستدعي وقتاً طويلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence mirrors the next verse: after forbidding distraction by wealth, the text puts charity first, since charity releases wealth from hand and heart; remembrance then corresponds to becoming righteous.
rows.anchor: ولما قدم النهي عن الإلتهاء بالمال قدم الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran generally puts wealth before children when distraction, adornment, or boasting is in view, but puts loved relatives first in the love-focused list in Tawbah.
rows.anchor: حيث اجتمع المال والولد في القرآن الكريم، قدم المال على الولد إلا في موطن واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Tawbah, relatives precede wealth because the context is love: close family together are dearer than money, which people spend on them and leave to them.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن المقام مقام حب. ولا شك أن المتقدمين من الأبناء والأزواج وغيرهم أحب إلى المرء من ألأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying whoever does that assigns the action to the person, affirming that distraction is within one's control and that one is responsible for it.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن ذلك بمقدور، وأن هذا من فعله وكسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense yaf'al signals the repeated, ongoing distraction that occurs day after day, unlike a one-time past action.
rows.anchor: الفعل المضارع الذي يدل على التكرار والتطاول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A past verb might suggest that even one occurrence brings the stated loss; the categorical nominal ending better fits recurring distraction and lasting loss.
rows.anchor: إنما يقع ولو فعله مرة واحدة وهو غير مراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them the losers fits people who seek profit through wealth: distraction is actually a loss, trading the lasting great for the trivial and perishable.
rows.anchor: حيث باع "العظيم الباقي بالحقير الفاني"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative, separating pronoun, and definite losers restrict and intensify the judgment: these people are the true and most complete losers.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أنهم هم الخاسرون دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Ruh al-Ma'ani likewise reads the demonstrative, restriction, repeated predication, and separating pronoun as emphatic.
rows.anchor: روح المعاني) : "وفي التعريف بالإشارة والحصر للخسران فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God is chosen because it encompasses every duty: worship is done for God through inward or spoken remembrance, including prayer, praise, and supplication.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن ذكر الله يشمل جميع الفرائض

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan glosses remembering God here as all the religious obligations.
rows.anchor: والتحميد وغير ذلك والدعاء وقال الحسن: جميع الفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to spend answers the hypocrites' command not to support the Messenger's companions, directly reversing their call to withhold charity.
rows.anchor: فانظر كيف قابل النهي بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive min asks for only some of one's wealth, easing people into giving instead of asking for everything and provoking miserliness.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن الإنفاق إنما يكون في قسم من المال ولا يشمل المال كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the wealth what We provided reminds people that it comes from God, its true provider, making them more willing to give some of it.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن هذا المال غنما هو من رزق الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min before death marks a time beginning near death, urging people to hasten good works because any passing hour could be their last; without min, the time could be distant.
rows.anchor: ومعناه الزمن القريب من الموت بل المتصل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object ahadakum precedes death to keep each person in focus as the one needing repentance, called to spend, and left regretting if death overtakes him.
rows.anchor: فالعناية والاهتمام منصبان على المفعول الذي يأتيه الموت، وهو كل واحد منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa in then he says conveys both cause and immediate sequence: death causes the plea for delay, which comes at once; thumma would imply delay and waw only conjunction.
rows.anchor: فجاء بالفاء لجمع معنيي السبب والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The urgent plea omits the vocative particle, saying Lord rather than O Lord, to save time and move straight to the request.
rows.anchor: لأن الوقت لم يعد يحتمل التضييع في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawla is a stronger, more insistent demand than law and also expresses regret; it better fits someone urgently asking for respite than a mild request or unattainable wish.
rows.anchor: وقائلها أكثر إلحاحاً من قائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past akhkhartani indicates that the fatal loss has already happened; a present verb could suggest the matter has not yet occurred and there is still time.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن المحذور وقع في حين أن الفعل المضارع قد يفيد أن الأمر لم يقع بعد
